messages:
Alex: Heads-up — p99 in eu-west jumped after we flipped cross-region fallback at 03:12 UTC. Baseline for model-rtx-small was ~320ms, now seeing ~720ms.
Divya: I see the same on the SLO dashboard. p95 is basically unchanged, tail took the hit.
Kai: Any quick hypotheses? Kernel change, batching, or KV behavior?
Alex: Quick trace from the routing/serve logs:```[03:12:07] route: eu-west -> us-east (fallback)
[03:12:07] kernel: aten_fast -> aten_quant_v2
[03:12:07] microbatch.size adaptive: 8 -> 16
[03:12:07] kv_cache.miss_rate: 0.18 -> 0.32```
Maria: looks like two amplifiers: (1) fallback routing sends traffic to a node that doesn't have warmed KV cache -> cold KV rebuilds; (2) the runtime's adaptive microbatcher grows batch size when throughput rises, adding queueing to already slower cross-region RTT.
Divya: kernel selection switching to aten_quant_v2 on the fallback path also matches a timeline where per-token latency increased ~0.9ms in our microbench. Combined with longer network RTTs, that pushes the tail up.
Kai: Can we quantify impact separately? e.g., simulate local kernel switch vs kv miss vs microbatch cap?
Alex: I ran quick canaries: (A) cap microbatch_size=8 for routed->fallback requests: p99 dropped 720 -> 380 ms, throughput -6%. (B) force local kernel (aten_fast) on fallback nodes: p99 dropped 720 -> 440 ms, throughput unchanged. (C) pre-warmed KV (warm for 60s): p99 dropped 720 -> 360 ms, throughput -3%.
Maria: interesting — KV pre-warm and microbatch cap both help; kernel pin helps but less than kv warm. Suggests miss amplification is the dominant factor.
Divya: tradeoff note: capping microbatch reduces batching efficiency (cost up slightly). If cross-region fallback rate > ~8-10% we hit SLO breach unless we change routing policy.
Kai: proposed short plan: 1) rollback adaptive microbatch growth for cross-region routed requests (cap at 8), 2) add KV pre-warm for top fallback targets (60s window), 3) pin kernel selection to the higher-performance path on fallback nodes while we stabilize, 4) add metrics/alerts: cross_region_pct, kv_miss_rate, p99_by_route, microbatch_size_hist.
Alex: I'll open a canary PR implementing caps + pre-warm. Can we do a staged canary to eu-west only? Need release window tonight. @Kai — can you coordinate canary?
Kai: Ack. I'll schedule a 30-minute canary for eu-west at 22:30 UTC. Will monitor p99 and cost.
PerfBot: Alert: p99 spike detected for model-rtx-small in eu-west at 03:12 UTC. Triggered automated rollback check: no auto-rollback configured for cross-region policy.
Maria: For the follow-up, let's also add a small perf test that simulates cross-region latencies (50-120ms additional RTT) to measure interplay with microbatcher and kv miss.
Divya: Agreed — we should also tweak rollout gating: if fallback rate > 5% during rollout, hold canary.
Alex: Thanks everyone — will post PR link and brief runbook in this thread once canary is up.
Kai: thumbs up :+1:
Alex: (will follow up)
